items.title: Detector dog sniffs out undeclared food at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Border services officers at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga, including a four-legged customs official, have seized another large shipment of undeclared food items being brought into Canada from abroad. The Canada Border Services Agency said the latest stash of undeclared food and animal products, which included 16 kilograms of goat feet, chicken, ghee and milk powder, was recently intercepted by CBSA detector dog Aggie. Agency officials said the undeclared items arrived on a flight at Pearson along with a group of travellers from Pakistan. The travellers were fined $1,350, the Canada Border Services Agency said. The incident is the latest seizure of meat, poultry and other food items made at Pearson and publicized by the CBSA in 2026. The Canadian government reminds travellers they are required by law to declare all food, plant and animal products being brought into the country. CBSA officials say failure to declare any of these products or to provide required permits/certificates can lead to: “Inadmissible goods may be confiscated and disposed of, or ordered removed from Canada,” the border services agency said in an online update to travellers.

items.title: New rental apartment building development nears completion in Mississauga
items.summary: A new rental building development is taking shape with occupancy expected to start next year in Mississauga. Dubbed “Boulevard on the Green,” the Morguard Corporation development at 725 Village Green Blvd. celebrated a topping-off ceremony this month. Topping-off typically refers to adding the last beam or roof component. In this case, the building was already fully enclosed, but Morguard created a ceremonial glass plaque and guests were invited to sign it, Brian Athey, senior vice president, development at Morguard, told INSAUGA Canada. The development, near Cawthra Road and Atwater Avenue, broke ground in October 2024. 7-acre property, just south of the Mississauga Seniors Centre, has been vacant for many years. The project includes three mid-rise buildings — one nine-storey and two eight-storey residential buildings along with townhomes. It will bring 431 new purpose-built rental units to Mississauga. The property’s zoning allowed for 12-storey buildings, but Athey said Morguard opted for a development that fit into the neighbourhood. The immediate area is mainly single-family homes and townhomes. “We’re trying to be sensitive to the neighbourhood context by not doing towers,” Athey said. Athey said that Morguard has owned the property for around 20 years. He believes the property had previously been home to a post office facility, possibly for sorting mail.

items.title: New mayor, city council will hold first meeting at Living Arts Centre in Mississauga
items.summary: It’s official. Mississauga has a new mayor, two first-time city councillors and nine other councillors who’ll return to represent their wards for another four years. Mississauga’s city clerk has certified the results of the 2026 municipal election, making them official, the City of Mississauga said Thursday morning. “Certification confirms the final election results after all votes have been counted and verified, as required by the Municipal Elections Act,” the city said in a news release. “Mississauga voters elected a mayor, 11 ward/regional councillors and school board trustees. ” The newly elected Mississauga city council, headed by mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, will meet for the first time on Nov. 16. m. During the ceremonial meeting, the new mayor and members of council will take their oaths of office and formally begin their term, which runs from 2026 to 2030. Tedjo, who’s moving from the Ward 2 council seat into the mayor’s office, and Mississauga city council will then quickly get down to business two days later at a general committee meeting to take place on Nov. 18. Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo and city council will be sworn in for the next term on Nov. 18 at the inaugural council meeting. Tedjo, whose poll numbers early in the mayoral campaign didn’t initially place him in contention with the incumbent Carolyn Parrish or her predecessor Bonnie Crombie, wound up decisively defeating the two political heavyweights on election night this past Monday.

items.title: Dense Fog Prompts Near-Zero Visibility Warning Across Mississauga and Nine Other Municipalities
items.summary: According to Environment and Climate Change Canada, a yellow-level weather advisory is in effect Thursday morning for Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon, Halton Hills, Burlington, Oakville, Newmarket, Georgina and northern York Region. The agency says areas of dense fog are expected to impact the region, with visibility suddenly dropping to near zero at times. Environment Canada reports travel will likely be hazardous in some locations as a result. The agency is advising drivers to prepare for near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach their destinations. According to Environment Canada, the fog is expected to dissipate later in the morning.

items.title: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga Introduces Guided Biofilm Therapy With Airflow Dental Cleaning in Mississauga
items.summary: Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is now offering Guided Biofilm Therapy as an additional professional dental cleaning option for patients in Mississauga. Mississauga, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 29, 2026) - Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga has added Guided Biofilm Therapy to its dental cleaning services, expanding the options available to patients during routine professional cleanings. The addition introduces airflow dental cleaning as part of the practice's preventive care services and gives the dental team another method to consider when planning a cleaning appointment. Professional cleanings are a regular part of dental care, but the approach used during an appointment can vary depending on the patient and the condition of the teeth and gums. By adding Guided Biofilm Therapy, Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga is giving patients more choice in how routine cleaning care may be approached while keeping the overall focus on oral health maintenance. Guided Biofilm Therapy uses airflow technology as part of the cleaning process and can be incorporated when appropriate. The service is not intended to replace every traditional cleaning method. Instead, it can be considered alongside other techniques based on what the dental team observes during the appointment. The addition also gives patients an opportunity to understand how their cleaning will be approached before treatment begins. Some patients may want to know why one method is being considered over another, while others may simply prefer to understand the options available to them. Offering GBT dental cleaning in Mississauga gives the practice a clearer way to explain those choices and discuss how Guided Biofilm Therapy may fit into an individual cleaning visit. For Caminschi Family Dentistry Mississauga, the new service expands its preventive dental care without changing the purpose of regular cleaning appointments.

items.title: Elliot Lake Drug Raid Nets Mississauga Man Among Two People Charged
items.summary: According to the Ontario Provincial Police, a Mississauga man is one of two people charged after officers executed a search warrant Tuesday night at an apartment in Elliot Lake, roughly 160 kilometres west of Sudbury. The OPP reports officers recovered a large quantity of hard drugs during the raid. According to police, the investigation involved the OPP's Community Street Crime Unit, Organized Crime Enforcement Bureau and the East Algoma detachment. The OPP identified the two people charged as 45-year-old Jennifer Stubbert of Elliot Lake and 20-year-old Kory Joseph-Labban of Mississauga. Police say both face numerous charges stemming from the drug seizure. According to the OPP, both were held in custody and scheduled to appear Wednesday in bail court at the Ontario Court of Justice in Blind River.
